Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray shows bilateral upper zone opacities (hypotransparency), but the opacity in the right hemithorax is visibly larger and more pronounced than on the left. This asymmetry, combined with the upper lobe predominance, suggests a progression or evolution of a process that may have initially presented as right-sided pneumonia, rather than a symmetric chemical injury or isolated lower lobe disease.
